classification.difficultyReason: Carry the common area through successive triangles, selecting perpendicular heights that include combined segments and sometimes lie outside the triangle.

content.prompt: The triangle below is divided into four smaller triangles of equal area. Find the values of $x$, $y$ and $z$.

spec.description: Four equal-area triangles identified by complete editable outlines and supplied side labels.
spec.mathematics: Four equal-area triangles with a right angle at the lower-left corner. Diagram coordinates are illustrative and are not printed measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and unknown labels are shown; connectivity point names remain unprinted.

answer.short:
$x=1$, $y=\frac12$, $z=\frac23$.

Compare the four triangle areas, each equal to $\frac12$.
answer.worked:
The bottom-left triangle has area $\frac{1\times1}{2}=\frac12$. Each smaller triangle therefore has area $\frac12$.

The next triangle has base $x$ on the vertical side and perpendicular height $1$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x\times1}{2}&=\frac12\\x&=1.\end{align*}$$
The triangle with base $y$ has perpendicular height $1+x=2$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{y\times2}{2}&=\frac12\\y&=\frac12.\end{align*}$$
The top triangle has base $z$ on the vertical side and perpendicular height $1+y=\frac32$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{z\times\frac32}{2}&=\frac12\\\frac{3z}{4}&=\frac12\\z&=\frac23.\end{align*}$$
